title: Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) Training Notes: Compounding of Later Distribution-Margin Rows Retired for an Estate
content:
# Compounding of Later Distribution-Margin Rows Retired for an Estate

*Training notes — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).*

**The rule.** The estate discount on a later distribution-margin allocation retired for an estate is compounded by the size of the row's gross: a gross under **$100.00** is compounded monthly at one twelfth of the adjusted rate; a gross of at least $100.00 and under **$1000.00** is compounded twice a year at one half of the adjusted rate; a gross of at least $1000.00 is compounded once a year.

## Questions answered

**Which gross decides the compounding?** The gross of the row as retired for the estate: the allocated amount of that year less every general retirement already booked on it, held within the room left under the estate annual cap for the calendar year, rounded to the cent.

**How is monthly compounding figured?** One plus one twelfth of the adjusted rate, as a decimal, is raised to the power of twelve times the horizon in years; the gross is divided by the result.

**Twice a year?** One plus one half of the adjusted rate is raised to the power of two times the horizon.

**Once a year?** One plus the adjusted rate is raised to the power of the horizon.

**Where do the edges fall?** $99.99 is compounded monthly; $100.00 and $999.99 twice a year; $1000.00 once a year.

## Worked figures (hypothetical adjusted rate of 5.5 percent, horizon of 6 years)

| Gross | Compounding | Divisor | Discounted value |
|---|---|---|---|
| $70.00 | monthly | 1.004583 raised to the power 72, which is 1.389920 | $50.36 |
| $450.00 | twice a year | 1.0275 raised to the power 12, which is 1.384784 | $324.96 |
| $1500.00 | once a year | 1.055 raised to the power 6, which is 1.378843 | $1087.87 |
